paper_title: DrainSinkhorn: Safe Elimination for Batched Entropic Optimal Transport

checks.accuracy_sweep_status: formal two-host EXP-PACKER19 stopping-execution Pareto with five residual tolerances and a separate seven-point native potential-threshold mapping
checks.local_tolerance_diagnostic_scope: superseded in the manuscript by EXP-PACKER19; C51 remains historical evidence only
checks.local_tolerance_cross_campaign_rule: EXP-PACKER19 consumer TV is computed within one campaign against its tight reference; no C51 values are combined with it
checks.accuracy_contract_provenance: archive/outdated_current_surface/20260906/root/todo_final.md at git commit 8b6cc50, committed before formal timing
checks.accuracy_contract_interpretation: project-defined consumer-output stability bound, not an external biological performance requirement
checks.method_hierarchy: DrainSinkhorn starts from standard fixed-width multi-problem Sinkhorn execution and the selected solver stopping rule. Its method contribution is dynamic compaction: after a problem passes that rule, all per-problem state is compacted and later updates run at survivor width A_k=|{t:ell_t>=k}|.
checks.safe_definition: stopping-rule-preserving release: a problem is removed only after passing the same configured two-marginal stopping check used by the selected backend; the one-marginal precheck only controls whether that existing check is invoked; the timed packed Triton path uses backend-supported precision
checks.component_ablation_interpretation: Matched fixed-width versus dynamic-compaction and logical-mask versus dynamic-compaction comparisons test the method contribution. Sequential versus fixed-width results measure conventional batching and are excluded from current-paper performance claims. EXP-PACKER19 static-derived ablations are ineligible and have been removed from the paper.

attribution_levels.ordinary_batching_context: project sequential per-problem versus fixed-width batched execution; prior capability excluded from current-paper performance claims
attribution_levels.dynamic_compaction: matched fixed-width or logical-mask execution versus dynamic compaction after the configured stopping rule

checks.c63_internal_decomposition: on real ImageNet-32 PCA500 training, the complete fixed-update E3 interval gives 1.03556x for fixed-width/dynamic-compaction, with observed three-seed range 1.02982--1.04311x; the separately recorded solver-field matched ratio is 1.053985x and remains a different timing scope

checks.algebraic_claim_scope: standard fixed-width batching applies the original independent per-instance Sinkhorn update in ideal arithmetic; the updated-marginal identity is also standard ideal-arithmetic algebra; neither is claimed as a new method
checks.numerical_claim_scope: the paper makes no new floating-point convergence or production-correctness theorem; it reports parity, achieved residuals, shadow replay, finite-precision stress tests, and application endpoints
checks.fp64_stress_test_scope: C10 is an independent numerical stress test: FP64 is a replay or audit reference, and the outward-bound plus FP64-escalation configuration is evaluated only within C10; neither FP64 replay nor escalation is included in the public-Flash timed application paths
checks.width_cost_role: the exact matched-path time difference maps verifier-derived survivor widths through a measured backend width-cost curve and subtracts incremental control overhead
checks.width_cost_diagnostic_scope: single-A100 primitive diagnostic for the packed Triton shifted_step at source commit 73aec2941bfa1a5caa6a6bddf7aa83b734f9bb8b; excludes screen, two-marginal verifier, compaction, and solve_batch outer loop
checks.end_to_end_scope: includes unchanged non-OT consumer, model, data, and training time; this dilutes the measured OT-stage gain
checks.packed_triton_role: compatible inner backend; no public serial performance ratio is used in the current paper
checks.cross_backend_realization_scope: OTT-JAX and PyKeOps validate backend-specific active-batch compaction; they do not reuse the Flash one-marginal precheck or Triton compaction kernel
checks.cross_backend_adaptation_claim: Packed Triton, OTT-JAX, and PyKeOps results show that active-batch compaction can be realized across the tested backend families; each performance statement remains within its registered backend and timing scope.
checks.cross_backend_optimization_headroom: further backend co-design can optimize fused phase execution, active-state layout, dynamic compaction, memory reuse, and backend-specific scheduling beyond the evaluated lightweight adapters
